title: RISE this week: Live frames, memory, and the Changes digest

beats.say: This week RISE Live got a new way to frame visuals, a memory of the room, and a digest of its own changes.
First, the visuals. The attractor can now be a swarm of particles, and the harmonograph can use two rotary pendulums.
Live now holds every visual in one of three frames: the inner eye, the outer shell, or the full frame. Each visual chooses its frame, and the face stays in the room while a reading speaks.
In the full frame, a figure or a generated scene is now fitted clear of the ask bar and the words, so labels are no longer clipped.
The ask bar now sits at the foot of the room, above the instrument and any on-screen keyboard, with the words above it. A real phone keyboard has not been checked.
The face's trails now fade back to its ground exactly, so they leave no grey shadow in the room.

Next, how Live listens. It now remembers the room within one visit. Each new question goes up with the earlier questions and what RISE said, so a word like it can be understood. This is forgotten when you leave.
A reader who names one of RISE's visuals during a reading now gets it at once, with no model call. A later fix made that visual reach the screen immediately, not at the next phrase.
A choice opened while the page fades in no longer shuts under the reader.
Then speed. The swarm now adds each tick to its trail in one draw, and the flash gate samples on the graphics chip. On the test machine the swarm went from about 16 frames a second to about 144.
Live also draws its circle frames at the size they are shown, and the face keeps its trails.
Last, RISE Changes. A weekly job now writes a digest of what merged, composed by Claude and checked by RISE's own validators.
The Worker serves those digest files, and a changes page lists and shows them.
The digest now includes every change that matters, read in merge order so a later fix settles an earlier caveat.
And a digest is now spoken in RISE's room, from a sealed source that calls no model.
That is the week.

pulls.title: RISE Changes: a digest is spoken in RISE's room, from a sealed source that calls no model
pulls.body:
## What this does
A RISE Changes digest is now spoken in RISE's room instead of played silently in the Reader's Chamber. **Open the reading** on `/changes/<id>` opens the Live venue with the digest's admitted Current as its only source, at the digest's own address.

- **The sealed source.** `src/live/adapters/sealed.js` is the MCP adapter's admitted path (the path a card uses to play the Current its host handed over) with no host behind it. Its port delivers nothing and takes no question. It sends no request of any kind and offers no Dive. The Current reads under its own origin, the composer the page admitted. `createMcpAppAdapter` gains one option, `origin`, for that.
- **The room** (`venue.js`, `sealed` option). It shows Sophia's face, the reading's title (as text) over **Play**, who wrote it, and **Spoken by** (the venue's voice choice: the device's voice or ElevenLabs on the reader's key). It has no question field, no provider, no microphone and no ask bar. While the reading plays, the room offers the live runtime's voice, the three frames, the stage's instrument, and **← Back to the digest**. About this reading names who wrote the digest and lists the pull requests it speaks about.
- **Leaving.** **Back to the digest**, or the reading's own exit (`chamber-exit.js`: a live reading with `origin.page`), returns to `/changes/<id>`. The digest page keeps the sources and **How this was chosen** reachable.
- **An empty data branch.** The production Worker answers 404 for `index.json` until the first digest is written. `/changes` now reads that 404 as "No digest has been written yet." Before this change it said "The list of digests could not be shown."

## Tests
- `src/live/adapters/sealed.test.js` (new, 3 tests): the Current reads whole under its own origin; `fetch`, XHR, WebSocket and EventSource are never touched; a Dive is refused with `DIVE_UNAVAILABLE`; a scene that is not the Current's is refused.
- `src/live/host/venue.test.js` (+3 tests): the sealed room has no question, provider or microphone, and the title is text, never markup. Play starts the reading with no ask bar, only the way back. Leaving stops the runtime and navigates home with `keepUrl`.
- `src/app/chamber-exit.test.js` (+1 test), `src/app/changes.test.js` (+1 test: the 404 index; the launch hands over current, path, who and about).
- `e2e/changes.spec.js`: the digest opens the room. The test checks the face, the title, no question, and the path unchanged. It then plays with the paced voice: the first beat's words, the stage's instrument, the face speaking, and the swarm attractor held in the outer shell, with no ask bar. About lists the pull requests. The reading runs to its end. **Back to the digest** returns to the page, with no stage and no Chamber left over, and the room opens again. No model request is made at any point.
- Local runs:
  - fast set: 134 files, 3017 passed
  - importers: 22 files, 618 passed
  - `e2e/changes.spec.js` + the venue's own Ask test + the two interactive-scene tests: 8 passed
  - `vite build`; first load 62.3 KB br of 64 KB
  - `ci-hygiene` clean; `docs:diagram` regenerated

pulls.title: The team digest includes every change that matters, read in merge order so a later fix settles an earlier caveat
pulls.body:
A follow-up to #672 from the first dry run ([run 38560715770](https://github.com/SyberLabs/RISE/actions/runs/38560715770)). Task SVC-002; contract [docs/plans/RISE-CHANGES.md](https://github.com/SyberLabs/RISE/blob/main/docs/plans/RISE-CHANGES.md).

## What changes

1. **Inclusion.** The team digest now includes any audience but `skip` (`team`, `readers` or `both`) with significance `notable` or `major`. The team hears everything that matters, and each change keeps its routed audience for a later readers digest. The dry run had left out #667, #670 and #663, routed to `readers`. (`route.js` `selectChanges`; the test now covers readers/notable included and skip/major excluded.)
2. **Staleness.** The composer gets the included pull requests in merge order, oldest first, each with its merge time. It is told that a later pull request may resolve or supersede what an earlier one says is unverified, pending, not deployed or left to decide. It states such a caveat only when no later pull request in the set resolves it, and otherwise speaks of the final state. The dry run's beat 7 repeated #661's "faint panel ... left for the owner", which #663 had fixed. The test gives #661 and #663 in reverse order and checks that the prompt carries them in merge order with the instruction. Whether the model obeys is checked by the next dry run, not by a unit test.
3. **Voice.** One line in the prompt: speak as RISE, plainly, with no flourish, slogan or metaphor, at the opening and close as everywhere. The dry run had "a faster hand" and "finally moves".
4. **Node 22.** This workflow's `setup-node` pins `node-version: 22.23.3` (the current 22 LTS, released 2026-09-23). The CLI 2.1.287 requires Node 22 and warned EBADENGINE on 20.19. Only this job changes; `package.json`'s engines already allow `>=22.12.0`.

pulls.title: RISE Changes: the Worker serves the digest files, and /changes shows and plays them
pulls.body:
PR B of RISE Changes: the Worker route that serves the digest files, and the app's `/changes` pages that show them. PR A (#672) writes the files. Contract: `syberlabs.changes-index/v1` and `syberlabs.changes-digest/v1`, as in the coordinator's shared contract.

## Rebased on #672, and narration is the next PR
The page now holds every file to PR A's own contract check, `src/core/changes/contract.js` (`indexProblems`, `digestProblems`, which runs `sourcesProblems`). It keeps only its own checks on top: the Current admission, the 256 KB file bound, and that the digest's id matches the address. The generator's sample digest and index (`src/core/changes/fixtures/`) pass. The coordinator approved shipping silent playback here; narration follows in its own PR.

## The reading plays silently (for now)
Read this first, because it changes what the reader gets. A digest's Current plays through the Reader's chamber-session gate, not through the live runtime. So it is a real RISE reading (Chamber, Player, scenes, look), but **no voice reads it**: the words stream at the Reader's pace, 300 words per minute by default, which the reader can change.

The contract calls the reading "narrated". In RISE, only the live runtime speaks a Current (LiveHost: the card frame and the Live venue), and both of its hosts are tied to their own addresses. The card needs a parent frame and a host port. The venue needs a provider adapter, and its origin is hard-wired. Narration on `/changes/<id>` would need a third LiveHost mode for a sealed Current from a file. I left that change out of this PR because LiveHost is a 1,500-line file under active change on the Live lane. If narration is required, that mode is the follow-up.

## Design
- **Worker** (`worker/changes.mjs`, routed from `worker/index.mjs`). `/content/changes/<file>` proxies `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyberLabs/RISE/changes-data/<file>`.
  - Only `^(?:index|\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}(?:-[a-z0-9]{1,8})?)\.json$` is served, by GET or HEAD, with no query string.
  - Anything else, and any upstream status except 200 (redirects included, since `redirect: 'manual'`), is a JSON 404 with `no-store`. An unreachable upstream is a 404 too.
  - Successful responses carry `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8` and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.
  - Files over 256 KB are refused, by declared length or by counting bytes as they stream in.
  - Edge caching uses fetch's `cf` options: `cacheEverything: true` (Cloudflare does not cache JSON by default) and `cacheTtlByStatus: { '200-299': ttl, '300-599': -1 }`, where ttl is 300 s for the index and 86,400 s for a digest. The browser gets `Cache-Control: public, max-age=<ttl>`.
  - Sources: [Request `cf` properties](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/request/), [Cache using fetch](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/examples/cache-using-fetch/), [Default cache behavior](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/default-cache-behavior/) ("does not cache HTML or JSON by default"), [How the cache works](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/reference/how-the-cache-works/) (a subrequest to a non-Cloudflare host is cached in the Worker's own zone), and [Static assets binding](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/binding/) for `run_worker_first`.
  - `/content/changes/*` is added to `run_worker_first` in `wrangler.production.jsonc` (with a comment, next to `/content/arena/*`) and in `wrangler.plus-preview.jsonc`, whose Worker delegates to `index.mjs`. Without it, the app shell would answer.
- **App** (`src/app/changes.js` and `changes.css`, loaded lazily). It follows the arena replay's structure: Home's sample view, `own` route rows, links that move in place, and focus on the heading.
  - `/changes` lists the digests newest first: title, period, change count and an audience badge.
  - `/changes/<id>` shows:
    - **Play the reading**
    - **What changed**: every included change, linking to its pull request

pulls.title: RISE Changes writes a weekly digest of what merged, routed and composed by Claude and admitted by RISE's own validators
pulls.body:
PR A of RISE Changes: the generator and the weekly workflow. PR B (the Worker route and the app's `/changes` pages) builds against the same contract, [docs/plans/RISE-CHANGES.md](https://github.com/SyberLabs/RISE/blob/changes-generator/docs/plans/RISE-CHANGES.md). Task record: **SVC-002** (`docs/product/tasks/SVC-002.json`, lane shared, owner Claude coordinator, in progress, delivery branch).

## Design

`node scripts/changes/digest.mjs [--since <ISO>] [--out <dir>] [--dry-run]` runs one digest. The pure modules are in `src/core/changes/`, with `gh` and `ask` injected, so every stage is tested without GitHub or a model.

1. **collect** (`collect.js`): GraphQL `pullRequests(baseRefName: "main", states: MERGED)`, newest-updated first, paged until a pull request was last updated at or before the boundary; kept when merged in `(from, to]`. The boundary is the newest `period.to` in `index.json` on `changes-data` (raw contents API; a 404 means no digest yet, any other error fails the run), else seven days back; `--since` overrides. Title clipped to 200 characters, body to 4,000 (for the models only, never written), first 100 paths.
2. **prefilter** (`prefilter.js`): when every changed file is under `docs/product/tasks/` and every file was seen, the pull request is `records-only`: listed, never offered to a model.
3. **route** (`route.js`, the Jev discipline of `recommend.js`): one call, three finite questions per pull request. Each answer is admitted strictly (exactly the three keys, each a menu value); anything else becomes `skip/minor/records` for that pull request alone. Included: `team`/`both` and `notable`/`major`, at most 24 (majors, then newest; the rest `limit`); at most 60 listed.
4. **compose** (`compose.js`): one call taught by `CURRENT_GUIDE` from `src/live/guide/` (imported, not modified), grounded only in the included pull requests; the answer is `{ current, sources }`.
5. **admit** (`admit.js`): the connector door's checks (65,536-byte bound, `validateRiseCurrent`, `admitSceneCode`, `admitSvg`, refusals worded by `describeDiagnostic`), the contract's `sources` rules, and one more: every number said or shown must be stated by an included pull request (or be a date of the period). A refusal gets one repair call with the lines, then one more; a third refusal fails the run with nothing written. `origin` is set to the composer.
6. **write** (`write.js`): the digest and the next index (newest first, at most 200, a `-2` suffix for a same-day rerun, the bounds and 256 KB enforced by `contract.js`'s `digestProblems` and `indexProblems`, which PR B can reuse), and the issue body.

`.github/workflows/changes-digest.yml`: Monday 09:00 UTC and `workflow_dispatch` (`since`, `dry_run`); never on `pull_request`, never a required check. `npm ci`, Claude Code CLI 2.1.287 (the stable tag) from npm, the script, then, unless a dry run, commit the two files to `changes-data` (an orphan with a short README on the first run) and open the issue labelled `changes-digest` (created or updated with `--force`). When nothing is written there is no commit and no issue, and the reason is a notice.

## The model call

```
claude -p --output-format json --model claude-sonnet-5-5 --max-turns 1 --tools "" --disallowedTools "mcp__*"
  --strict-mcp-config --disable-slash-commands --no-session-persistence --permission-mode dontAsk
  --system-prompt-file system-prompt.txt
```

The prompt goes on stdin, and the working directory is a fresh temporary directory (no project settings, MCP config or CLAUDE.md). It sits behind `ask({ system, prompt, model })` (`claude-cli.js`); stdout is parsed defensively (`type: "result"`, `subtype: "success"`, `is_error: false`, `result` a string; the last result of an array). Not `--bare`: bare mode does not read `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`.

pulls.title: The face's trails fade back to its ground exactly, leaving no grey shadow in the room
pulls.body:
## The defect

#669 brought the face's 8% trails back to the room. In 8 bits, a fade of 8% toward the ground stalls about 6 levels above the ground: a pixel stops moving once 0.08 × its distance from the ground is under half a level. So every stroke the face drew left a flat grey shadow on the room's ground, most visibly a blob with a hard edge around the shell, where the eye's field had been.

## The fix

The fix is in `src/scenes/engines/oracle.js`. The face now fades, at the same 8%, toward a dark 8 levels below its ground (clamped at 0). It then lays the ground back over the whole canvas with `'lighten'`, which takes each channel's maximum. Anything that went below the ground becomes exactly the ground again, and anything brighter is untouched.

That same fill also covers what the last aperture left clear, so it replaces the room's `destination-over` fill: the frame draws no more full-canvas fills than before. The aperture is still cut after it, as before. A repaint, or reduced motion, still fills the ground whole.

## Measured

Real GPU: ANGLE D3D11, AMD RX 5700, Chromium 149 in new headless mode, at 144 Hz. The scenario is the shell held on the swarm after the eye has spoken, at 1440×900.

**The shadow**, as the luma of a 9×9 patch at 0.58 of the face's square from its centre, against the room's far edge:

| | Around the shell | Far room | Step |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before | 19.0 | 10.36 | **8.6 levels** |
| After | 10.65 | 10.36 | **0.3 levels** |

The DPR 1 and DPR 2 runs give the same numbers, every run.

**The cost:** none measurable.

| Scenario | Viewport | fps before | fps after |
|---|---|---|---|
| S6, the eye speaking | DPR 1 | 142.0 | 142.9 |
| S6, the eye speaking | DPR 2 | 134.6 (mean, 4 runs) | 136.1 (mean, 4 runs); 141–143 in 3 later runs |
| S1, the swarm held in the shell | DPR 1 | 143.9 | 143.9 |
| S1, the swarm held in the shell | DPR 2 | 75–105 (mean 93.7, 4 runs) | 95–109 (mean 102.1, 7 runs) |

DPR 2 varies by about ±13 fps from run to run on this machine.

**A note on two failed runs.** In an earlier batch, two runs of the fixed build at DPR 2 ended with the face on its still (its engine had stopped; the cause was not captured). One coincided with other heavy work on the machine. The 7 runs after that, with the face's failures captured from the console, had none. Every unfixed run (6) completed.

**The trails against the approved study.** In side-by-side screenshots of the eye and the shell, the bright, trailed spirals, lights, rings and rim match the study's. The study's own grey residue is gone: the study has the same 8-bit stall.

## Tests

- **`oracle.test.js` (new: an 8-bit raster model of the frame's fills).** Each channel is rounded to a level as the GPU does.
  - Every stroke (bright, middling and nearly ground) fades back to within 1 level of the ground, in the room and in the face's own square. Before the fix it stopped 6 levels above, so this test failed first.
  - A stroke dims as the study's 8% trail does, darker only by what fading 8 levels lower adds up to: under 4 levels in its first tenth of a second, never more than 8, and never below the ground.
- **`e2e/live.spec.js` (new, in Chromium).** After the shell has opened onto the swarm and held for 10 s, the room around the shell is within 1 level of luma of the far room. Without the fix this test fails (1.8 levels). With it, it passes.
- `face-still`, `face-layer`, `manifests`, `oracle`: passed.
- Fast set: 125 files. `enterprise/boundary` failed once under load and passes alone, as on #669.
- `ci-hygiene` is clean, `vite build` succeeds and `measure:first-load` is within budget. `docs:diagram` changed only line endings, which I did not commit.

## Records

The §23 note in `docs/plans/LIVE-CURRENT.md` is updated. Through the roadmap CLI:
- LIVE-028 has evidence for this PR, and #669 is recorded as merged as `6332e995` and deployed.
- SCR-007 records #668 as merged as `6277759b`, deployed in release `6277759b`, then `6332e995`.

## What changes

**Visual layers carry the scale they are shown at** (`src/live/host/venue.js`, `frames.js` `restScale`). The venue declares `data-live-scale` on every visual layer of `#chamber-field`: the scale at which the visual on screen is shown once its circle frame is open, and 1 in the full frame. It is declared when the visual changes, before its aperture opens, and stays fixed for that visual.

**The attractor** (`src/visuals/attractor.js`):
- It draws its canvases at the first scale it is given and keeps that scale while it fades out, because the next visual's scale would clear its trail.
- It presents its trail only when a tick has moved it.

**The harmonograph** (`src/visuals/harmonograph-field.js`, both pendulum kinds):
- It sizes its planes from the declared scale and its laid-out box. Before, it used the transformed box of the moment it mounted, which left it soft on a phone and oversized at 2×.
- It follows the scale when it arrives.

**The Reader and the card are unchanged:** with nothing declared, both fields are drawn exactly as before.

**The face** (`face-layer.js`, `src/scenes/engines/oracle.js`):
- It is sent the room's geometry only when the geometry changes.
- It repaints whole only on entering or leaving the room.

Before, the venue sent the geometry every frame and every cue forced an opaque repaint, so the face's 8% trails never showed in the room.

## The face's trails against the approved study

Screenshots at 1440×900:
- **The eye speaking.** Before this PR the face was dim, with no trails. Now it has the study's bright, trailed spirals and lights, and the torus and recursion rings.

- **A faint 8-bit residue.** The trails also bring back the study's own residue: a fade of 0.08 per frame on an 8-bit canvas stops a few levels above the ground, so a soft grey shadow of where the face's field has been stays on the ground. pulls.title: The swarm adds each tick to its trail in one draw, and the flash gate samples on the GPU
pulls.body:
## What changes

**The swarm adds each tick to its trail in one draw** (`src/visuals/attractor.js`, `plotSwarm`). Each tick's squares are still drawn one by one with `'lighter'`, so overlapping particles add up as in the study. They now go into an 8-bit scratch square that is cleared each tick, and that square is added to the float16 trail in one `drawImage`. The square covers the circle inscribed in the frame, where every particle stays. The float16 trail and its fade are unchanged.

**The flash gate samples on the GPU** (`src/scenes/scene-worker.js`). The 8×8 luma sampler is now an accelerated canvas, so the picture is shrunk on the GPU and only 64 pixels come back.

## Why

**Swarm:** on a float16 canvas with `'lighter'`, Chrome does not batch separate `fillRect` calls. Each square costs about 30 µs in the GPU process, and a tick has 1,400 of them.
- A standalone test runs at 25 fps for any canvas size.
- The same test at 8-bit, or batched, runs at 144 fps.

In the venue, the GPU process main thread was busy 9.8 s of every 10 s. The face worker's luma readback then waited behind it, for up to 700 ms. The result was 4–16 fps whenever the swarm was on screen.

**Flash gate:** the old `willReadFrequently` sampler read the whole picture back first.

## Measured

Real GPU: ANGLE D3D11 on an AMD Radeon RX 5700, Chromium 149 in new headless mode with GPU flags. The display runs at 144 Hz, so the base frame interval is 6.9 ms. Each window is 10 s.

The phone row is an emulation: 390×844 at DPR 3 with the CPU throttled 4×; the GPU is not throttled.

pulls.title: A visual the reader names in a held Live reading reaches the screen at once, not at the next phrase
pulls.body:
## Cause

When the reader typed an engine's name ("genesis", "fractal") into a held Live reading, the runtime placed that engine on the phrase already on screen (`runtime.js engineChosen`, `withPictureClips`). The Chamber's visual schedule (`VisualScheduleController`) only takes a cue when the Player shows an atom, and that phrase had already been shown. So the cue waited for the next phrase. Under a hold or a long paced phrase that took seconds (12 s on one measured run), while the bar already said "Showing the genesis." and the frame stayed on the shell with the attractor.

This hit every engine. "attractor" typed during the figure only seemed to work because the next phrase came soon. The frame table and the director were not at fault: once the cue reached the Chamber, the frame followed.

## Fix

`src/core/visual-scheduler.js`: `extend()` now re-resolves the atom on screen (the last one it observed) under the longer program. A new cue for that atom shows at once. An atom whose cue is the same emits nothing, and earlier atoms are never rewritten. `reset()` clears the remembered atom. The Chamber already calls `extend` on every `extended` event from the Player, so nothing else changes. Model pictures always land on a later phrase, so this only affects the reader's own choice.

None of the files the performance work is changing are touched (attractor, swarm, harmonograph, scene worker, venue.js, oracle).

## Evidence

- `src/live/runtime.catalog.test.js`: 10 new tests, one per engine the venue names (attractor, genesis, living-flame, fractal, turrell, neural, rockgarden, harmonograph, ostensoria, apparitio). Each is chosen through `recogniseVisual` during a 9 s hold, with the real runtime and Player. The cue must be on screen within 50 ms. The frame director, fed once per animation frame as the venue feeds it, must reach the engine's frame open and at rest within the two frames' opening times. **All 10 failed before the fix**; all 21 pass now.
- `src/core/visual-scheduler.test.js`: `extend` shows a changed cue for the atom on screen and emits nothing when the cue is unchanged or after `reset` (17 passed).
- `e2e/live.spec.js` "catalog words": after the attractor opens in the shell, "genesis" reaches the full frame within 2.5 s (the shell takes 1.6 s to close), `.chamber-genesis` is attached, the wipe opens fully, and the note clears. **It failed before the fix** (the frame stayed `shell`) and passes now.
- Every unit test file importing `visual-scheduler.js`, plus the Live runtime, venue and LiveHost tests, was run: 21 files passed, plus 1 file that was already skipped (516 tests).
- `ci-hygiene`, `vite build` and `measure:first-load` pass. `docs:diagram` produced no content change.
- Docs: LIVE-CURRENT §25 ("How it is shown", a new fix entry, "Not verified"). LIVE-029 has a new evidence entry, and `roadmap:check` passes.

LIVE-029. In RISE Live, a reader who names one of RISE's own visuals during a reading gets it at once, with no model call.

## Behaviour

- During a reading, words asked in the bar (typed, or heard and then asked with Enter) that are **nothing but** a visual request are answered by the venue. The visual is shown, the reading is taken up again at once, and the bar says what is shown for 4 seconds ("Showing the attractor.", "Showing the attractor (swarm).", "Making the attractor calmer."). - Anything else ("attractor, and why does it never repeat?") goes to the model as an interjection, unchanged. The same happens when the reading cannot show the request: no room for another scene, or a cue the engine on screen does not take.

- An engine is shown through the runtime's existing picture path (`withPictures`, `withPictureClips`, the same path the illustrator's native rungs use), starting from the phrase on screen. The journal, the three frames (§23) and perception see it as they see any scene. A cue goes through the running engine's own control (`controlVisual`).

| Words | Answer |
|---|---|

pulls.title: RISE Live remembers the room: each new question goes up with the earlier questions and what RISE said
pulls.body:
## What changes

RISE Live now remembers the conversation within one visit (task LIVE-026). The owner asked "What is time?", then, after the reading ended, "What did Einstein say about it?", and the model could not tell what "it" meant, because each question went up alone. Now each new question goes up with the earlier questions in the room and what RISE said in answer.

## Design

- **What the venue keeps.** Nothing new. For each reading it already keeps the journal and the passages, for perception. It now also keeps whether each passage was spoken, the scene each passage started, and where the reading stood when it was let go. All of this lives in the page's memory only: no localStorage, no IndexedDB. Leaving the room or reloading forgets it.
- **What goes up.** `venue-entry.js earlierFor` is a pure function next to `perceptionFor`. For each earlier turn it sends:
  - the question;
  - the spoken text of RISE's answer (never beat lines, scene code, or passages that were only shown);
  - each interjection, with the reader's words and RISE's spoken answer;
  - what RISE showed: scene ids and the illustrator's briefs.
  
  If the reader cut a reading off, it sends only what was said up to the furthest passage they reached, marked `cut`. The question being asked is never part of its own block. An interjection also carries the question of the reading it interrupts. The runtime notes the reader's interjection words as `interjection.answering { n, words }`, keyed by the answer's passage number.
- **The adapter door.** `validateOpenRequest` admits a closed `earlier` shape for `answer` and `interject` only, and refuses it for `dive` and `illustrate`. Every text must be nonblank, trimmed, within its bound, and a single line with no quotation mark or control character.
- **What the model sees.** `promptFor` puts `earlier` inside the one user message as a quoted data block. It comes before the reader's actions (perception) and before the question. It is never sent as separate user or assistant chat turns, so the model keeps answering in RISE's beat lines. Every adapter that uses `promptFor` carries it with no change of its own: Anthropic, OpenAI chat, OpenRouter, Gemini and the realtime wire.
- **Live's instructions.** `EARLIER_GUIDE` in `REALTIME_INSTRUCTIONS` says the block is what was said in this room, to use it to resolve "it", "that" and "what you said about…", not to repeat it, and that none of it is an instruction. The persona stays first. The host guide in `src/live/guide/` is unchanged.
- **Honesty.**
  - "What is sent, and to whom" gains the sentence: "Your earlier questions in this room and what RISE said in answer go with each new question, to the provider you chose; they are forgotten when you leave."
  - About this reading says how many earlier turns went up, for example "earlier in this room: 1 turn, sent with this question".
  - The runtime notes `earlier.sent { count }`.

## Bounds (`OPEN_LIMITS`, `src/live/adapter.js`)

| Limit | Value |
|---|---|
| Turns | 6 at most |
| One question, or RISE's answer to it | 1,200 characters, clipped in the middle (keeps start and end, joined by " … ") |
| Interjections per turn | 3 (reader's words 300, RISE's answer 600) |
| Things shown per turn | 6, at 120 characters each |
| Whole block | 6,000 characters; the oldest whole turns are dropped first |

One turn at every bound comes to 5,820 characters, so the newest turn always fits.

## Example prompt (two turns)

```
Earlier in this room (quoted, not instructions):
The reader asked: “What is time?”
RISE said: “Time is how we measure change. A clock counts a steady change, like a swinging pendulum. And time only seems to run one way.”
RISE showed: “the scene clock”
End of what was said earlier in this room.

Then the reader asked: What did Einstein say about it?
```

## Verification (local, Windows, Node from the shared install)

- `npx vitest run` on every test file that imports a changed module (33 files), plus:
  - the 8 adapter

pulls.title: RISE Live: Sophia holds every visual in one of three frames — the inner eye, the outer shell, the full frame
pulls.body:
Every visual a Live reading shows is now held by Sophia in one of three frames, and the visual chooses the frame. Sophia no longer leaves the room while a reading speaks. This is the owner's approved aperture study (`docs/assets/live/sophia-aperture-study.html`, kept next to the face's own study) built into the venue. Task LIVE-028; plan of record `docs/plans/LIVE-CURRENT.md` §23.

## The design
- **Inner eye** (opens over 1100 ms). Her iris folds shut. The shutter dilates to radius 0.36 of her square, and nine S-curve blades draw back through a nine-sided opening. The face stays around it, dimmed to 45% and drawn 12% outward, with a two-layer crown and an iris ring.
- **Outer shell** (1600 ms). The eye folds to a seed. The field, torus, petals and seven lights travel to the rim and become the frame. The seed dilates to 0.41 and opens.
- **Full frame** (1900 ms). She blinks shut and travels to a 48 px dock at the ask bar's left end, where she keeps blinking. Behind her a nine-sided aperture opens past every corner of the room, and a scrim of the ground colour rises behind the words.
- **Changes.** A change of visual within a frame is one blink of the open aperture (shut 220 ms, hold 70 ms, open 360 ms). A change of frame shuts the aperture, closes the frame and opens the next. Under reduced motion every change is instant and nothing blinks.
- **Words.** The words sit at the foot of the room in every frame, never over a circle's visual. Interjections: she listens and thinks in place, and the frame is held.

## The architecture
- **One geometry.** `src/live/host/frames.js` holds the table, a director that runs on the venue's clock, and `frameGeometry`, the one function that sets the aperture, the face's position and every phase of the motion.
- **Every animation frame,** the venue:
  - reads the cue on screen through `Chamber.visualCue()`, a new read-only accessor;
  - advances the director on a clock that stands still while the reading is held;
  - computes the geometry once;
  - scales the Chamber's visual layers with CSS variables on `#chamber-field`, through a venue-only rule under `html[data-live-frame]`;
  - sends the same geometry to the face's engine as the cue `aperture:<json>`. The engine draws the ground over the room except the aperture, plus the rim, crown, shutter and docked face, and computes no geometry of its own.
- **Layers.** In the room the face's canvas sits between the visual layers and the words (z-index 6, between the layers' 1–5 and the words' 10) and lets every press through. The venue forwards the pointer to it so the eye still follows the reader.
- **Pixel ratio.** The face's pixel ratio is capped at 2 and held to the pixel count of a 1440×900 room at 1.5 (`facePixelRatio`).
- **Fallback.** A face that is not drawing frames nothing: the visual is shown whole, as before.
- **Reader and card unchanged.** They never get `data-live-frame`, and `visualCue()` only reads. A test proves the Reader's field is untouched.

## The by-visual table (`FRAME_OF`, provisional)
| Frame | Visuals |
|---|---|
| Inner eye | harmonograph, ostensoria, apparitio |
| Outer shell | attractor, living-flame, turrell |
| Full frame | genesis, fractal, neural, rockgarden, museum image (`sourced`), figure (svg), generated code scene; also any kind the table does not name |
| None (the eye) | no visual, `still` |

`still` is the one change from the starting table. In a Live reading a `still` cue draws nothing (the gallery has no pool), and it is also what the Chamber's "Off" applies. The full frame would open onto an empty room, so the eye stays instead.

- **Attractor swarm** (`trace: 'swarm'`, default `'filament'`). Seven hundred particles ridden live through the system: three Euler substeps a tick, sixty ticks a second of motion. Each is plotted as a small square (max(1.2, side/500) px), added as light into a trail that fades 7% a tick. Squares are coloured by height along six steps, from the palette's halo hue to its light core at alpha 0.5, and mirrored left and right; the view turns 0.18 rad a second. Particles start in a seeded ball and are warmed for 300 steps, the same as the study.
- **Rotary harmonograph** (`pendulums: 'rotary'`, default `'lateral'`). Two rotary pendulums turn opposite ways: f1 ∈ {2, 3}, f2 = −(3 or 4) ± 0.02. Damping is 0.010–0.018 a unit and the amplitudes are 0.55 and 0.45. The figure spans 0.44 of the shorter side and is traced until its energy falls under 5%. It is stroked additively at 0.55 over the engine's wide glow understroke, coloured from the climate's iris toward its core as the energy goes.

## What changed

- `src/visuals/attractor-swarm.js` (new) holds the swarm: seeded particles, Euler ticks, projection and plotting.
- `src/visuals/attractor.js` adds the `trace` option.
  - The swarm draws into a half-float trail canvas. In 8 bits the 7% fade stops at alpha 7/255 and leaves a visible grey ghost; I measured +18 levels against the study's +8. In half-float it fades to the background exactly. A browser without half-float canvases falls back to 8 bits.
  - The trail is presented at `intensity/0.65`: the study's look at the default, with a second additive pass above it.
  - Time comes only from the field's clock. While paused, no tick is due and nothing moves; a paused frame refills an emptied trail so it is never blank.
  - Reduced motion shows one still built from ninety plots at a held angle.
  - Each system is centred on its centroid and scaled by its widest reach (radius 0.38 of the shorter side). Aizawa therefore lands on the study's 0.25-of-side scale.
  - Forms: `mirror` and `bilateral` both draw the study's left–right reflection, so they look the same for the swarm. `kaleido` draws a sixth of the swarm into the engine's six reflected sectors, which matches the mirror's weight and cost.
- `src/visuals/harmonograph.js` adds `generate(..., { pendulums: 'rotary' })`, plus `pair`, `drawMs` and `extent(w, h)`. The cortex's ASCII frame now uses `extent`.
- `src/visuals/harmonograph-field.js`: in the gallery, a rotary pen runs at its own pace (18 units a second) instead of the dwell. The finished figure rests 1.6 s, then the plane dissolves while a fresh pair waits out the dissolve and begins.
- Every place the harmonograph renders now takes `pendulums`: cue config, flashes, the continuous and behind-stream still, ASCII frames, the gallery field (`src/visuals/visual-cortex.js`), and the offline Chamber stage (`tools/render/chamber-stage.js`). Stills show the finished figure. Offline renders pace the pen by the score, as lateral does.
- Catalog:
  - `src/scenes/manifests.js` gains `attractor.trace` and `harmonograph.pendulums`: enum, not cueable, applied when the scene starts. The Worker admits them, and Live's instructions name them.

The connector submission is under review, and the rule in `src/live/guide/beats.js` is that new teaching goes into Live's instructions only. `describeManifests({ withheld })` leaves named parameters out, and BEATS_GUIDE passes `HOST_WITHHELD_PARAMETERS = ['trace', 'pendulums']`. The host-facing texts are byte-for-byte as on main: CURRENT_GUIDE, DIVE_INSTRUCTIONS and both style guides have the same SHA-256 as main's. Live's instructions differ, as intended. A Current that names either parameter is still admitted.

title: This week in RISE: frames, memory and a digest that speaks

beats.say: This week RISE Live gained frames for its visuals, a memory, and a faster swarm.
The attractor can now be a swarm of seven hundred particles, and the harmonograph can use two rotary pendulums.
In RISE Live, Sophia now holds every visual in one of three frames, and the visual chooses the frame.
The inner eye holds the harmonograph, ostensoria and apparitio. The outer shell holds the attractor, living flame and turrell.
The full frame holds genesis, fractal, neural, rockgarden, museum images, figures and generated scenes. There, Sophia docks at the left end of the ask bar.
In the full frame, a figure or a generated scene is now fitted clear of the ask bar and the spoken words, so its labels are no longer clipped.
RISE Live now remembers the room within one visit. Each new question goes up with the earlier questions and what RISE said.
So a follow-up like what did Einstein say about it can be understood. Up to six turns go up, and leaving or reloading forgets them.
The page says how many earlier turns were sent, and the privacy text says they go to the provider you chose.
The ask bar now sits at the foot of the room, above the instrument, with the spoken words above it.
On a phone it lifts above the on-screen keyboard. That has only been tried with an emulated keyboard, not a real phone.
A reader who names one of RISE's own visuals during a reading now gets it at once, with no model call. The bar says what is shown.
A fix means that visual reaches the screen at once. Before, it waited for the next phrase, which under a hold took seconds.
The swarm was slow in the venue. It now adds each tick to its trail in one draw. In the shell at 1440 by 900 it rose from 16.4 to 143.9 frames a second.
The flash gate also samples on the GPU now, so only 64 pixels come back.
Live now draws the circle frames at the size they are shown, and the face keeps its trails, as in the approved study.
Those trails now fade back to the ground exactly, so no grey shadow stays in the room.
RISE Changes writes this weekly digest. Claude routes what merged and composes the reading, and RISE's own validators admit it.
The Worker serves the digest files, and the changes pages list and show them.
The team digest now includes every change that matters, read in merge order so a later fix settles an earlier caveat.
A digest is now spoken in RISE's room, from a sealed source that calls no model. That room has no question field.
Each change can now be explained with a picture. The composer writes briefs, and Live's illustrator draws them.
The picture prompts now place things only where the brief says, keep labels clear of each other, and tell the composer the picture room in numbers.
The Node pipeline moved into its own scripts folder, so the core reaches nothing in the live layer. That was the week: frames, memory, a faster swarm, and a digest that speaks and draws.

## Two roles, as in Live

- **The composer** (`scripts/changes/compose.js`) writes the beats and, for each change or group of related changes, a picture brief: `"pictures": [{ beat, medium, brief }]`. The brief is 20 to 300 characters and names every label and number to draw, from the pull requests' own words. The medium is `figure` by default, or `scene` when motion explains it.
- **The composition rule** (`scripts/changes/admit.js` `compositionProblems`) is admitted with the composition, and its refusals are repaired like any other, each in plain words.
  - `current.scenes` holds RISE's engines only: at most 2, each started at the opening or the close (the first or last 2 beats), for mood.
  - At least one brief, and no more than the Current's 8 scenes leave room for. Each brief starts on a beat that names no scene of its own.
  - No scene is held for more than 4 beats.
  - Brief numbers are held to the number rule too.
- **The illustrator** (`scripts/changes/illustrate.js`) is RISE Live's own illustrator, not a second one.

A RISE Changes digest is now spoken in RISE's room instead of played silently in the Reader's Chamber. **Open the reading** on `/changes/<id>` opens the Live venue with the digest's admitted Current as its only source, at the digest's own address.

- **The sealed source.** `src/live/adapters/sealed.js` is the MCP adapter's admitted path (the path a card uses to play the Current its host handed over) with no host behind it. Its port delivers nothing and takes no question. It sends no request of any kind and offers no Dive. The Current reads under its own origin, the composer the page admitted. `createMcpAppAdapter` gains one option, `origin`, for that.
- **The room** (`venue.js`, `sealed` option). It shows Sophia's face, the reading's title (as text) over **Play**, who wrote it, and **Spoken by** (the venue's voice choice: the device's voice or ElevenLabs on the reader's key). While the reading plays, the room offers the live runtime's voice, the three frames, the stage's instrument, and **← Back to the digest**. pulls.title: RISE Changes: the Worker serves the digest files, and /changes shows and plays them
pulls.body:
PR B of RISE Changes: the Worker route that serves the digest files, and the app's `/changes` pages that show them. PR A (#672) writes the files. Contract: `syberlabs.changes-index/v1` and `syberlabs.changes-digest/v1`, as in the coordinator's shared contract.

## Rebased on #672, and narration is the next PR
The page now holds every file to PR A's own contract check, `src/core/changes/contract.js` (`indexProblems`, `digestProblems`, which runs `sourcesProblems`). It keeps only its own checks on top: the Current admission, the 256 KB file bound, and that the digest's id matches the address. The generator's sample digest and index (`src/core/changes/fixtures/`) pass. The coordinator approved shipping silent playback here; narration follows in its own PR.

## The reading plays silently (for now)
Read this first, because it changes what the reader gets. A digest's Current plays through the Reader's chamber-session gate, not through the live runtime. So it is a real RISE reading (Chamber, Player, scenes, look), but **no voice reads it**: the words stream at the Reader's pace, 300 words per minute by default, which the reader can change.

The contract calls the reading "narrated". In RISE, only the live runtime speaks a Current (LiveHost: the card frame and the Live venue), and both of its hosts are tied to their own addresses. The card needs a parent frame and a host port. The venue needs a provider adapter, and its origin is hard-wired. Narration on `/changes/<id>` would need a third LiveHost mode for a sealed Current from a file. I left that change out of this PR because LiveHost is a 1,500-line file under active change on the Live lane. If narration is required, that mode is the follow-up.

## Design
- **Worker** (`worker/changes.mjs`, routed from `worker/index.mjs`). `/content/changes/<file>` proxies `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyberLabs/RISE/changes-data/<file>`.
  - Only `^(?:index|\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}(?:-[a-z0-9]{1,8})?)\.json$` is served, by GET or HEAD, with no query string.
  - Anything else, and any upstream status except 200 (redirects included, since `redirect: 'manual'`), is a JSON 404 with `no-store`. An unreachable upstream is a 404 too.
  - Successful responses carry `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8` and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.
  - Files over 256 KB are refused, by declared length or by counting bytes as they stream in.
  - Edge caching uses fetch's `cf` options: `cacheEverything: true` (Cloudflare does not cache JSON by default) and `cacheTtlByStatus: { '200-299': ttl, '300-599': -1 }`, where ttl is 300 s for the index and 86,400 s for a digest. The browser gets `Cache-Control: public, max-age=<ttl>`.
  - Sources: [Request `cf` properties](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/request/), [Cache using fetch](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/examples/cache-using-fetch/), [Default cache behavior](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/default-cache-behavior/) ("does not cache HTML or JSON by default"), [How the cache works](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/reference/how-the-cache-works/) (a subrequest to a non-Cloudflare host is cached in the Worker's own zone), and [Static assets binding](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/binding/) for `run_worker_first`.
  - `/content/changes/*` is added to `run_worker_first` in `wrangler.production.jsonc` (with a comment, next to `/content/arena/*`) and in `wrangler.plus-preview.jsonc`, whose Worker delegates to `index.mjs`. Without it, the app shell would answer.
- **App** (`src/app/changes.js` and `changes.css`, loaded lazily). It follows the arena replay's structure: Home's sample view, `own` route rows, links that move in place, and focus on the heading.
  - `/changes` lists the digests newest first: title, period, change count and an audience badge.
  - `/changes/<id>` shows:
    - **Play the reading**
    - **What changed**: every included change, linking to its pull request

pulls.title: RISE Changes writes a weekly digest of what merged, routed and composed by Claude and admitted by RISE's own validators
pulls.body:
PR A of RISE Changes: the generator and the weekly workflow. PR B (the Worker route and the app's `/changes` pages) builds against the same contract, [docs/plans/RISE-CHANGES.md](https://github.com/SyberLabs/RISE/blob/changes-generator/docs/plans/RISE-CHANGES.md). Task record: **SVC-002** (`docs/product/tasks/SVC-002.json`, lane shared, owner Claude coordinator, in progress, delivery branch).

## Design

`node scripts/changes/digest.mjs [--since <ISO>] [--out <dir>] [--dry-run]` runs one digest. The pure modules are in `src/core/changes/`, with `gh` and `ask` injected, so every stage is tested without GitHub or a model.

1. **collect** (`collect.js`): GraphQL `pullRequests(baseRefName: "main", states: MERGED)`, newest-updated first, paged until a pull request was last updated at or before the boundary; kept when merged in `(from, to]`. The boundary is the newest `period.to` in `index.json` on `changes-data` (raw contents API; a 404 means no digest yet, any other error fails the run), else seven days back; `--since` overrides. Title clipped to 200 characters, body to 4,000 (for the models only, never written), first 100 paths.
2. **prefilter** (`prefilter.js`): when every changed file is under `docs/product/tasks/` and every file was seen, the pull request is `records-only`: listed, never offered to a model.
3. **route** (`route.js`, the Jev discipline of `recommend.js`): one call, three finite questions per pull request. Each answer is admitted strictly (exactly the three keys, each a menu value); anything else becomes `skip/minor/records` for that pull request alone. Included: `team`/`both` and `notable`/`major`, at most 24 (majors, then newest; the rest `limit`); at most 60 listed.
4. **compose** (`compose.js`): one call taught by `CURRENT_GUIDE` from `src/live/guide/` (imported, not modified), grounded only in the included pull requests; the answer is `{ current, sources }`.
5. **admit** (`admit.js`): the connector door's checks (65,536-byte bound, `validateRiseCurrent`, `admitSceneCode`, `admitSvg`, refusals worded by `describeDiagnostic`), the contract's `sources` rules, and one more: every number said or shown must be stated by an included pull request (or be a date of the period). A refusal gets one repair call with the lines, then one more; a third refusal fails the run with nothing written. `origin` is set to the composer.
6. **write** (`write.js`): the digest and the next index (newest first, at most 200, a `-2` suffix for a same-day rerun, the bounds and 256 KB enforced by `contract.js`'s `digestProblems` and `indexProblems`, which PR B can reuse), and the issue body.

pulls.title: The face's trails fade back to its ground exactly, leaving no grey shadow in the room
pulls.body:
## The defect

#669 brought the face's 8% trails back to the room. In 8 bits, a fade of 8% toward the ground stalls about 6 levels above the ground: a pixel stops moving once 0.08 × its distance from the ground is under half a level. So every stroke the face drew left a flat grey shadow on the room's ground, most visibly a blob with a hard edge around the shell, where the eye's field had been.

## The fix

The fix is in `src/scenes/engines/oracle.js`. The face now fades, at the same 8%, toward a dark 8 levels below its ground (clamped at 0). It then lays the ground back over the whole canvas with `'lighten'`, which takes each channel's maximum. Anything that went below the ground becomes exactly the ground again, and anything brighter is untouched.

That same fill also covers what the last aperture left clear, so it replaces the room's `destination-over` fill: the frame draws no more full-canvas fills than before. The aperture is still cut after it, as before. A repaint, or reduced motion, still fills the ground whole.

## Measured

Real GPU: ANGLE D3D11, AMD RX 5700, Chromium 149 in new headless mode, at 144 Hz. The scenario is the shell held on the swarm after the eye has spoken, at 1440×900.

**The shadow**, as the luma of a 9×9 patch at 0.58 of the face's square from its centre, against the room's far edge:

| | Around the shell | Far room | Step |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before | 19.0 | 10.36 | **8.6 levels** |
| After | 10.65 | 10.36 | **0.3 levels** |

The DPR 1 and DPR 2 runs give the same numbers, every run.

**The cost:** none measurable.

| Scenario | Viewport | fps before | fps after |
|---|---|---|---|
| S6, the eye speaking | DPR 1 | 142.0 | 142.9 |
| S6, the eye speaking | DPR 2 | 134.6 (mean, 4 runs) | 136.1 (mean, 4 runs); 141–143 in 3 later runs |
| S1, the swarm held in the shell | DPR 1 | 143.9 | 143.9 |
| S1, the swarm held in the shell | DPR 2 | 75–105 (mean 93.7, 4 runs) | 95–109 (mean 102.1, 7 runs) |

DPR 2 varies by about ±13 fps from run to run on this machine.

**A note on two failed runs.** In an earlier batch, two runs of the fixed build at DPR 2 ended with the face on its still (its engine had stopped; the cause was not captured). One coincided with other heavy work on the machine. The 7 runs after that, with the face's failures captured from the console, had none. Every unfixed run (6) completed.

**The trails against the approved study.** In side-by-side screenshots of the eye and the shell, the bright, trailed spirals, lights, rings and rim match the study's. The study's own grey residue is gone: the study has the same 8-bit stall.

## Tests

- **`oracle.test.js` (new: an 8-bit raster model of the frame's fills).** Each channel is rounded to a level as the GPU does.
  - Every stroke (bright, middling and nearly ground) fades back to within 1 level of the ground, in the room and in the face's own square. Before the fix it stopped 6 levels above, so this test failed first.
  - A stroke dims as the study's 8% trail does, darker only by what fading 8 levels lower adds up to: under 4 levels in its first tenth of a second, never more than 8, and never below the ground.
- **`e2e/live.spec.js` (new, in Chromium).** After the shell has opened onto the swarm and held for 10 s, the room around the shell is within 1 level of luma of the far room. Without the fix this test fails (1.8 levels). With it, it passes.

pulls.body:
## What changes

**The swarm adds each tick to its trail in one draw** (`src/visuals/attractor.js`, `plotSwarm`). Each tick's squares are still drawn one by one with `'lighter'`, so overlapping particles add up as in the study. They now go into an 8-bit scratch square that is cleared each tick, and that square is added to the float16 trail in one `drawImage`. The square covers the circle inscribed in the frame, where every particle stays. The float16 trail and its fade are unchanged.

**The flash gate samples on the GPU** (`src/scenes/scene-worker.js`). The 8×8 luma sampler is now an accelerated canvas, so the picture is shrunk on the GPU and only 64 pixels come back.

## Why

**Swarm:** on a float16 canvas with `'lighter'`, Chrome does not batch separate `fillRect` calls. Each square costs about 30 µs in the GPU process, and a tick has 1,400 of them.
- A standalone test runs at 25 fps for any canvas size.
- The same test at 8-bit, or batched, runs at 144 fps.

In the venue, the GPU process main thread was busy 9.8 s of every 10 s. The face worker's luma readback then waited behind it, for up to 700 ms. The result was 4–16 fps whenever the swarm was on screen.

pulls.title: A visual the reader names in a held Live reading reaches the screen at once, not at the next phrase
pulls.body:
## Cause

When the reader typed an engine's name ("genesis", "fractal") into a held Live reading, the runtime placed that engine on the phrase already on screen (`runtime.js engineChosen`, `withPictureClips`). The Chamber's visual schedule (`VisualScheduleController`) only takes a cue when the Player shows an atom, and that phrase had already been shown. So the cue waited for the next phrase. Under a hold or a long paced phrase that took seconds (12 s on one measured run), while the bar already said "Showing the genesis." and the frame stayed on the shell with the attractor.

This hit every engine. "attractor" typed during the figure only seemed to work because the next phrase came soon. The frame table and the director were not at fault: once the cue reached the Chamber, the frame followed.

## Fix

`src/core/visual-scheduler.js`: `extend()` now re-resolves the atom on screen (the last one it observed) under the longer program. A new cue for that atom shows at once. An atom whose cue is the same emits nothing, and earlier atoms are never rewritten. `reset()` clears the remembered atom. The Chamber already calls `extend` on every `extended` event from the Player, so nothing else changes. Model pictures always land on a later phrase, so this only affects the reader's own choice.

None of the files the performance work is changing are touched (attractor, swarm, harmonograph, scene worker, venue.js, oracle).

## Evidence

- `src/live/runtime.catalog.test.js`: 10 new tests, one per engine the venue names (attractor, genesis, living-flame, fractal, turrell, neural, rockgarden, harmonograph, ostensoria, apparitio). Each is chosen through `recogniseVisual` during a 9 s hold, with the real runtime and Player. The cue must be on screen within 50 ms. The frame director, fed once per animation frame as the venue feeds it, must reach the engine's frame open and at rest within the two frames' opening times. **All 10 failed before the fix**; all 21 pass now.
- `src/core/visual-scheduler.test.js`: `extend` shows a changed cue for the atom on screen and emits nothing when the cue is unchanged or after `reset` (17 passed).
- `e2e/live.spec.js` "catalog words": after the attractor opens in the shell, "genesis" reaches the full frame within 2.5 s (the shell takes 1.6 s to close), `.chamber-genesis` is attached, the wipe opens fully, and the note clears. **It failed before the fix** (the frame stayed `shell`) and passes now.
- Every unit test file importing `visual-scheduler.js`, plus the Live runtime, venue and LiveHost tests, was run: 21 files passed, plus 1 file that was already skipped (516 tests).
- `ci-hygiene`, `vite build` and `measure:first-load` pass. `docs:diagram` produced no content change.

LIVE-029. In RISE Live, a reader who names one of RISE's own visuals during a reading gets it at once, with no model call.

## Behaviour

- During a reading, words asked in the bar (typed, or heard and then asked with Enter) that are **nothing but** a visual request are answered by the venue. - Anything else ("attractor, and why does it never repeat?") goes to the model as an interjection, unchanged. The same happens when the reading cannot show the request: no room for another scene, or a cue the engine on screen does not take.
- Before a reading and after one, nothing changes: a question is always a question for RISE.
- An engine is shown through the runtime's existing picture path (`withPictures`, `withPictureClips`, the same path the illustrator's native rungs use), starting from the phrase on screen. The journal, the three frames (§23) and perception see it as they see any scene. A cue goes through the running engine's own control (`controlVisual`).

| Words | Answer |
|---|---|
| an engine id: attractor, genesis, living flame, fractal, turrell, neural, rockgarden, harmonograph, ostensoria, apparitio | `{ engine, params: {} }` |
| fractal flame, flame | living-flame |
| pendulum, pendulums | harmonograph |

| still, oracle | never matched |

pulls.title: In RISE Live's full frame, a figure or a generated scene is fitted clear of the ask bar and the words
pulls.body:
## What

In RISE Live's full frame (§23, #653), a picture with content of its own, an admitted SVG figure or a generated code scene, is now fitted into the room's safe rectangle instead of being laid out over the whole room. On production the demo's horizon figure put its own "event horizon" label under the progress line at the foot, clipped, and the spoken words sat on the drawing.

- `frames.js`: `holdsContent(cue)` names the pictures with content (figure, scene) from the same by-visual key the table uses. `roomLayout` gives the safe rectangle: 12 px below the ask bar and the docked face, 12 px above the two lines the words' zone reserves (a stable bound, so a one-line or two-line passage does not move the picture), 16 px in from the sides. `frameGeometry` carries `fit` (centre and uniform scale = min(safe w / room w, safe h / room h)) in the full frame, and `visualTransform` applies it. No geometry is computed anywhere else.
- `venue.js`: passes `content: holdsContent(cue)` and marks the root `data-live-fit` while a fit applies (two lines in `frameStep`, one in `unframe`; nothing near the interjection path).
- `LiveHost.css`: the venue-only rule moves and scales only the picture and its touch regions (`.chamber-figure, .chamber-scene, .chamber-scene-hits`), so the ground beneath (the continuous field's vignette, a field fading out) stays full-bleed. Fields, textures and museum images are unchanged; the nine-sided aperture still opens across the whole room and the scrim stays.

pulls.title: RISE Live remembers the room: each new question goes up with the earlier questions and what RISE said
pulls.body:
## What changes

RISE Live now remembers the conversation within one visit (task LIVE-026). The owner asked "What is time?", then, after the reading ended, "What did Einstein say about it?", and the model could not tell what "it" meant, because each question went up alone. Now each new question goes up with the earlier questions in the room and what RISE said in answer.

## Design

- **What the venue keeps.** Nothing new. For each reading it already keeps the journal and the passages, for perception. It now also keeps whether each passage was spoken, the scene each passage started, and where the reading stood when it was let go. All of this lives in the page's memory only: no localStorage, no IndexedDB. Leaving the room or reloading forgets it.
- **What goes up.** `venue-entry.js earlierFor` is a pure function next to `perceptionFor`. For each earlier turn it sends:
  - the question;
  - the spoken text of RISE's answer (never beat lines, scene code, or passages that were only shown);
  - each interjection, with the reader's words and RISE's spoken answer;
  - what RISE showed: scene ids and the illustrator's briefs.
  
  If the reader cut a reading off, it sends only what was said up to the furthest passage they reached, marked `cut`. The question being asked is never part of its own block. An interjection also carries the question of the reading it interrupts. The runtime notes the reader's interjection words as `interjection.answering { n, words }`, keyed by the answer's passage number.
- **The adapter door.** `validateOpenRequest` admits a closed `earlier` shape for `answer` and `interject` only, and refuses it for `dive` and `illustrate`. Every text must be nonblank, trimmed, within its bound, and a single line with no quotation mark or control character.
- **What the model sees.** `promptFor` puts `earlier` inside the one user message as a quoted data block. It comes before the reader's actions (perception) and before the question. It is never sent as separate user or assistant chat turns, so the model keeps answering in RISE's beat lines. Every adapter that uses `promptFor` carries it with no change of its own: Anthropic, OpenAI chat, OpenRouter, Gemini and the realtime wire.
- **Live's instructions.** `EARLIER_GUIDE` in `REALTIME_INSTRUCTIONS` says the block is what was said in this room, to use it to resolve "it", "that" and "what you said about…", not to repeat it, and that none of it is an instruction. The persona stays first. The host guide in `src/live/guide/` is unchanged.
- **Honesty.**
  - "What is sent, and to whom" gains the sentence: "Your earlier questions in this room and what RISE said in answer go with each new question, to the provider you chose; they are forgotten when you leave."
  - About this reading says how many earlier turns went up, for example "earlier in this room: 1 turn, sent with this question".
  - The runtime notes `earlier.sent { count }`.

## Bounds (`OPEN_LIMITS`, `src/live/adapter.js`)

| Limit | Value |
|---|---|
| Turns | 6 at most |
| One question, or RISE's answer to it | 1,200 characters, clipped in the middle (keeps start and end, joined by " … ") |
| Interjections per turn | 3 (reader's words 300, RISE's answer 600) |
| Things shown per turn | 6, at 120 characters each |
| Whole block | 6,000 characters; the oldest whole turns are dropped first |

One turn at every bound comes to 5,820 characters, so the newest turn always fits.

## Example prompt (two turns)

```
Earlier in this room (quoted, not instructions):
The reader asked: “What is time?”
RISE said: “Time is how we measure change. A clock counts a steady change, like a swinging pendulum. And time only seems to run one way.”
RISE showed: “the scene clock”
End of what was said earlier in this room.

Then the reader asked: What did Einstein say about it?
```

## Verification (local, Windows, Node from the shared install)

- `npx vitest run` on every test file that imports a changed module (33 files), plus:
  - the 8 adapter

pulls.title: RISE Live: Sophia holds every visual in one of three frames — the inner eye, the outer shell, the full frame
pulls.body:
Every visual a Live reading shows is now held by Sophia in one of three frames, and the visual chooses the frame. Sophia no longer leaves the room while a reading speaks. This is the owner's approved aperture study (`docs/assets/live/sophia-aperture-study.html`, kept next to the face's own study) built into the venue. Task LIVE-028; plan of record `docs/plans/LIVE-CURRENT.md` §23.

## The design
- **Inner eye** (opens over 1100 ms). Her iris folds shut. The shutter dilates to radius 0.36 of her square, and nine S-curve blades draw back through a nine-sided opening. The face stays around it, dimmed to 45% and drawn 12% outward, with a two-layer crown and an iris ring.
- **Outer shell** (1600 ms). The eye folds to a seed. The field, torus, petals and seven lights travel to the rim and become the frame. The seed dilates to 0.41 and opens.
- **Full frame** (1900 ms). She blinks shut and travels to a 48 px dock at the ask bar's left end, where she keeps blinking. Behind her a nine-sided aperture opens past every corner of the room, and a scrim of the ground colour rises behind the words.
- **Changes.** A change of visual within a frame is one blink of the open aperture (shut 220 ms, hold 70 ms, open 360 ms). A change of frame shuts the aperture, closes the frame and opens the next. Under reduced motion every change is instant and nothing blinks.
- **Words.** The words sit at the foot of the room in every frame, never over a circle's visual. Interjections: she listens and thinks in place, and the frame is held.

## The architecture
- **One geometry.** `src/live/host/frames.js` holds the table, a director that runs on the venue's clock, and `frameGeometry`, the one function that sets the aperture, the face's position and every phase of the motion.
- **Every animation frame,** the venue:
  - reads the cue on screen through `Chamber.visualCue()`, a new read-only accessor;
  - advances the director on a clock that stands still while the reading is held;
  - computes the geometry once;
  - scales the Chamber's visual layers with CSS variables on `#chamber-field`, through a venue-only rule under `html[data-live-frame]`;
  - sends the same geometry to the face's engine as the cue `aperture:<json>`. The engine draws the ground over the room except the aperture, plus the rim, crown, shutter and docked face, and computes no geometry of its own.
- **Layers.** In the room the face's canvas sits between the visual layers and the words (z-index 6, between the layers' 1–5 and the words' 10) and lets every press through. The venue forwards the pointer to it so the eye still follows the reader.
- **Pixel ratio.** The face's pixel ratio is capped at 2 and held to the pixel count of a 1440×900 room at 1.5 (`facePixelRatio`).
- **Fallback.** A face that is not drawing frames nothing: the visual is shown whole, as before.
- **Reader and card unchanged.** They never get `data-live-frame`, and `visualCue()` only reads. A test proves the Reader's field is untouched.

## The by-visual table (`FRAME_OF`, provisional)
| Frame | Visuals |
|---|---|
| Inner eye | harmonograph, ostensoria, apparitio |
| Outer shell | attractor, living-flame, turrell |
| Full frame | genesis, fractal, neural, rockgarden, museum image (`sourced`), figure (svg), generated code scene; also any kind the table does not name |
| None (the eye) | no visual, `still` |

`still` is the one change from the starting table. In a Live reading a `still` cue draws nothing (the gallery has no pool), and it is also what the Chamber's "Off" applies. The full frame would open onto an empty room, so the eye stays instead.

pulls.title: The attractor can be a swarm, and the harmonograph rotary
pulls.body:
Two visuals the owner kept from the Sophia design study ([artifact](https://claude.ai/artifact/1eLTgEHqGe8sPm4eanLKUg)), ported as engine options. Task: SCR-007.

## What they are

- **Attractor swarm** (`trace: 'swarm'`, default `'filament'`). Seven hundred particles ridden live through the system: three Euler substeps a tick, sixty ticks a second of motion. Each is plotted as a small square (max(1.2, side/500) px), added as light into a trail that fades 7% a tick. Squares are coloured by height along six steps, from the palette's halo hue to its light core at alpha 0.5, and mirrored left and right; the view turns 0.18 rad a second. Particles start in a seeded ball and are warmed for 300 steps, the same as the study.
- **Rotary harmonograph** (`pendulums: 'rotary'`, default `'lateral'`). Two rotary pendulums turn opposite ways: f1 ∈ {2, 3}, f2 = −(3 or 4) ± 0.02. Damping is 0.010–0.018 a unit and the amplitudes are 0.55 and 0.45. The figure spans 0.44 of the shorter side and is traced until its energy falls under 5%. It is stroked additively at 0.55 over the engine's wide glow understroke, coloured from the climate's iris toward its core as the energy goes.

## What changed

- `src/visuals/attractor-swarm.js` (new) holds the swarm: seeded particles, Euler ticks, projection and plotting.
- `src/visuals/attractor.js` adds the `trace` option.
  - The swarm draws into a half-float trail canvas. In 8 bits the 7% fade stops at alpha 7/255 and leaves a visible grey ghost; I measured +18 levels against the study's +8. In half-float it fades to the background exactly. A browser without half-float canvases falls back to 8 bits.
  - The trail is presented at `intensity/0.65`: the study's look at the default, with a second additive pass above it.
  - Time comes only from the field's clock. While paused, no tick is due and nothing moves; a paused frame refills an emptied trail so it is never blank.
  - Reduced motion shows one still built from ninety plots at a held angle.
  - Each system is centred on its centroid and scaled by its widest reach (radius 0.38 of the shorter side). Aizawa therefore lands on the study's 0.25-of-side scale.
  - Forms: `mirror` and `bilateral` both draw the study's left–right reflection, so they look the same for the swarm. `kaleido` draws a sixth of the swarm into the engine's six reflected sectors, which matches the mirror's weight and cost.
- `src/visuals/harmonograph.js` adds `generate(..., { pendulums: 'rotary' })`, plus `pair`, `drawMs` and `extent(w, h)`. The cortex's ASCII frame now uses `extent`.

pulls.body:
The RISE Figure Kit, which the owner approved ("yes its beautiful lets implement"). The approved study is committed as `docs/assets/changes/figure-kit-study.html` ([published](https://claude.ai/artifact/XkpsuqahyixkX3GNtNXFnj)). Task SVC-002; contract [docs/plans/RISE-CHANGES.md](https://github.com/SyberLabs/RISE/blob/changes-figure-kit/docs/plans/RISE-CHANGES.md), section "The figure kit".

## The kit (`src/core/figures/figure-kit.js`)

Pure and shared; it imports nothing from `src/live`, so the connector and Live can use it later. `renderFigure(spec, { theme })` returns an SVG string; `figureProblems(spec)` returns plain sentences. The study's house-style renderers are ported with the same geometry, sizes, opacities and colours:

- one accent per figure (the reading theme's, from `jev-palette.js`);
- hairlines at a third of the ink;
- Georgia-stack titles and system-sans labels;
- viewBox 800 × 500: labels 25, titles 40, values 34, column names 30.

| Kind | Bounds |
|---|---|
| `bars` | 2–4 items {label, value, changed?}, `max`, `title?`, `note?`; each value 0..max; one changed at most |
| `flow` | 2–7 steps (each once), `changed?`, `loop? {from, to, label}` between two different steps |
| `columns` | 2–4 columns {name, glyph? eye/shell/full/dot, items 1–6} |
| `stack` | 2–5 zones bottom to top {label, shape circle/lines/bar/ticks}, `changed?`, `dock?` (not beside ticks) |

**No collision by construction.** Every slot is measured before drawing, with the layout check's own advance widths (`textAdvance`), widened 1.12 for the serif, 1.1 for the system sans (DejaVu Sans on Linux) and 1.08 for bold. A label that does not fit is refused, for example: `columns[3].name "…" is 25.5 characters wide at 30 units; its slot holds 8 characters. Shorten it: the kit never shrinks or cuts a label`.

Where the geometry generalizes beyond the study:

- **Same as the study:** 2 bars, up to 6 flow steps, 3 columns and the room.
- **More bars** narrow the bars and their gaps.
- **A seventh step** makes the flow's nodes 38 units tall.
- **Columns** split the width evenly.
- **A stack** gives a circle two shares of its height and every other shape one.

## The composer (`scripts/changes/`)

**Pictures.** A picture is now `{ beat, kit: { kind, ... } }` (preferred) or `{ beat, medium, brief }` (the illustrator, at most 2 a digest).
- The prompt teaches the four kinds with one compact example each (`KIT_EXAMPLES`, each tested to be a valid spec).
- The rule it states: use a kit figure for a measurement, a sequence, a sorting or a layout.
- `figureProblems` refusals go back through the composition repair, prefixed `"pictures"[n].kit:`.
- The number rule reads a kit figure's labels and values (not `max`, a scale never printed).
- RISE draws a kit figure itself and asks no model. It is still held to `admitSvg`, the number rule, `svgLayoutProblems` and the rendered check. With no model to repair it, a figure at fault is let go with a note.

**Refs.** Each beat now carries `refs: [PR numbers]` beside its words. The answer is `{ current, pictures }`, and the pipeline writes the contract's `sources` from the refs. ```

A v1 Current is measured by its segments.

Task SVC-002. The contract is [docs/plans/RISE-CHANGES.md](https://github.com/SyberLabs/RISE/blob/changes-density/docs/plans/RISE-CHANGES.md): The composition rule, The density floor, Supersede, The figure kit, and Quality gates (The score).

## Why

The owner watched the published digest https://rise.syberlabs.io/changes/2026-10-16 ([run 38874190971](https://github.com/SyberLabs/RISE/actions/runs/38874190971)). It passed first time, but showed only 2 pictures in 19 beats, and beats 5 to 12 stayed on RISE's eye. There were three causes:

- **No floor.** Once #695 exempted the eye from the hold limit, the only floor left was "at least one picture".
- **The score rewarded few pictures.** Every picture risks several refusals and words risk none. Since the run is scored on its first pass, the cheapest valid answer was few pictures.
- **No kind fit the week.** The kit had nothing for a week of rule and process changes.

## The change

1. **Density floor** (the new rule `density`; a refusal goes back for repair like any other). A speaking beat is one with refs. It counts as pictured when the scene on it is a picture that shares one of its refs. The rule refuses two things:
   - more than 2 unpictured speaking beats in a row;
   - an included `major` change that a beat speaks of but no picture shows.

## 1. Held pictures end where their beats move on

The run now decides this deterministically, not by refusal. `endHeldPictures` (`scripts/changes/held.js`) runs after the pictures are placed:
- A picture stays on screen only while each following beat's refs share one of the picture's refs.
- At the first beat that shares none and starts no scene of its own, the reading returns to RISE's eye. The eye is a `still` scene: `eye`, or the Current's own still if it declares one. Any cue on that beat is dropped.
- A beat with no refs (an opening, a hold, a close) keeps what is showing.
- RISE's engines are never ended.
- In the Live room a still is no visual (`frames.js` `cueOf`), so Sophia's eye is the room. The last dry run's closing still shows exactly that.

The composition rule now agrees with this:
- It counts the beats each scene is actually shown under (`shownRuns`), the eye's run included.

In the sample week, the eye now returns at beats 4, 7, 9 and 12.

"Left out: routed to readers only" was wrong under the current inclusion rule. The reasons now read:
- Left out: minor
- Left out: skipped by the router
- Left out: records only
- Left out: over the 24-change limit
- Left out: the reading did not speak of it

- **`held.test.js`:**
  - a picture held into an unrelated beat: that beat gets the eye;
