pulls.title: The Image Stream presenter: a fixation-size stream behind a flag that is off (RDR-031, step 2)
pulls.body:
Step 2 of the Image Stream (RDR-031; `docs/specs/IMAGE-STREAM-SPEC.md` §8): the presenter, behind a new build flag `IMAGE_STREAM_ENABLED = false`. **With the flag off no reader can reach the stream through any path, and `FLASHING_ENABLED` is untouched and stays false.** This PR does not turn flashing imagery on for anyone. It builds the part whose safety can be tested, keeps it unreachable, and writes down what must be true before the flag may flip.

## What is built

- **The flag and the surface.** `IMAGE_STREAM_ENABLED` beside `FLASHING_ENABLED`; `'stream'` joins `PRESENTATION_SURFACES` in the same change. `presentationFlashes('stream')` is true, so every gate that asks "does this flash" answers yes, and with the flag off `normalizePresentation('stream')` and every hostile input resolve to Gallery, even if the old event economy were switched back on. The only caller of the switchable normaliser is a test.
- **The presenter** `src/visuals/image-stream.js`: one canvas, at most 140 × 140 CSS px, frame replaces frame with no clear, fill or fade, only opaque frames, free-running, paused with the reading; every frame is held exactly the same whole number of refreshes and never replaced sooner than 1000/hz ms of real time.
- **The meter is armed at every size, not exempted by geometry.** Independent review showed the "small aperture is safe by size" argument fails in ordinary use: browser zoom, pinch, OS magnifiers and the glass tile's backdrop blur all enlarge the lit area without the page seeing it. So the runtime meter judges every frame at no less than 64× the safe area, multiplied by the device pixel ratio; a change over about 1.6% of the aperture (306 of 19,600 pixels) counts, and a 12 Hz black/white strobe trips it within half a second at any size. Zoomed pages are refused at mount, and a change in zoom, device pixel ratio or pinch stops the stream. Any trip, any exception (a tainted canvas), a stall over 500 ms, a refresh rate that disagrees with the measured one, photosensitivity or reduced-motion switching on (including while paused), or the end of consent stops it for good and hands the aperture back to Gallery.
- **Every off path stops it.** The reader's visual Off, a look change, any non-Gallery cue, Follow text, the Live venue's shut eye, a held scene and an Off already in force at launch revoke the stream for the reading; it can come back only through a new launch that raises the notice again.
- **The launch gate.** With the flag on, a reading asking for `'stream'` goes through the existing photosensitivity notice and fail-closed consent first (photosensitivity mode is now checked before any earlier consent); declining gives Gallery. The visual engine is never handed `'stream'`; Composer Currents cannot name it under any look.
- **Bounds.** At most 24 frames, a 5 s decode timeout, an 8-megapixel cap checked before decode, a rejected load is caught; the meter and `certifySequence` throw on non-finite time, mismatched arrays, an empty reel or a bad frame duration instead of passing.

## What this does not claim

Nothing here is a safety guarantee. Real reels of unrelated pictures will almost always trip the meter and fall back to Gallery until the reel compiler normalises luminance. An OS magnifier above about 2.5× over the glass tile remains a residual risk. The zoom heuristic misreads `outerWidth` in some browsers and would fail open inside a card or iframe. The spec's new section "Before IMAGE_STREAM_ENABLED may flip" lists eight preconditions (the reel compiler, the phone aperture, a decision on magnifiers, removing the backdrop blur from the aperture while the stream runs, measuring the blur footprint in a real browser, verifying the zoom heuristic in real browsers, the notice wording, and a real-browser safety review), and a test fails if that list is dropped. Nothing ran in a real browser.

pulls.title: The Image Stream core: a flash meter that measures light, and the stream's clock (RDR-031)
pulls.body:
The core of the Image Stream: rapid serial presentation of images, frame replacing frame, governed by the light it puts on the screen rather than by how often something is shown. It is the owner's route to bringing flashing imagery back (RDR-031). Nothing here can reach a reader: no `'stream'` surface is registered and nothing imports the meter yet.

## Why this and not the old switch

The retired Rhythmic mode is an event economy: at each atom boundary it pauses the words and flashes one image, so every event is itself a WCAG flash, and the only safety lever was making events rarer. That cannot express a stream, and making it safe meant `FLASHING_ENABLED = false`, which stays false and correct for that economy. The Image Stream limits risk by measuring light. Design, safety rules and the order of work are in `docs/specs/IMAGE-STREAM-SPEC.md`.

## What is built

- **`src/core/luminance.js`**: summarises a frame as a coarse grid of mean relative luminance and saturated-red values, averaged in linear light (WCAG 2.3.1 formulas).
- **`src/core/flash-meter.js`**: counts general and red flashes as WCAG defines them, tracking each cell's turning points so a slow dissolve is one transition and many small steps cannot hide a large swing. A transition only counts when the area changing exceeds the safe area (21,824 CSS px², about 147 px square). RISE allows two flashes in any second, one inside WCAG's three. `certifySequence` plays a reel through a fresh meter for at least two loops, so the wrap from last frame to first is checked. A stream inside the safe area cannot produce a countable flash at all (`apertureIsInherentlySafe`): the first presenter's safety will be geometry, not analysis.
- **`streamFrameAt`** in `visual-presence.js`: the stream's clock, 4 to 12 images per second (8 by default), each frame held for a whole number of display refreshes.
- `flashing-disabled.test.js` lists `'stream'` among the hostile inputs that must never flash.

## Not built, in order (spec §8)

2. The presenter at fixation-aperture size, free-running, behind its own flag. 3. The reel compiler. 4. The wide-field regime, runtime meter fallback and a stripe-pattern check (luminance arithmetic does not catch dense regular patterns). 5. The panel control and the photosensitivity notice. The stream stays opt-in behind the notice even when certified, because software cannot see panel brightness, HDR mapping or viewing distance.

## Verification

31 new tests (luminance, the meter, the stream clock); the meter was broken on purpose five ways and the tests caught four, the fifth change being harmless. The fast suite, hygiene check, architecture diagram, production build and first-load budget pass.

The Mystery School is the owner's graded canon of 66 public-domain texts (plan of 2026-10-13, now a dated record at `docs/product/discussions/2026-10-13-mystery-school-plan.md`): one Gate text, seven planetary houses with three degrees each, and five reading paths that cut across the houses. The school shows every text in one of three honest states resolved from the content manifest at runtime: *Readable in RISE*, *Carried, not served* (with the archive's reason), or *Not yet carried* (with the free edition named and a way to find it outside RISE). Admitting a text is a data change: set `work.id` on its record.
- **The Gate text cannot be read.** Pico's *Oration* has no free English edition; the Gate is the charter and the reader's seat, and the Oration stands at the centre marked as the school's first commission.

- **The Wheel**: one circle. The Gate at the centre; the seven houses as sectors in the Chaldean cycle clockwise from the Sun at the top; the three degrees as rings climbing outward (Threshold, Core, Arcanum); every text a point in its sector at its ring, with ink for its state (hollow, dashed, solid ring, ring with a dot for begun, filled for read, halo for a held arcanum). **Before.** The shell closed through its drawn-in seed and then regrew it to the eye's normal size. Only then did the glide shrink her again. In the eye-size curve this shows as a stop and a reversal.

**After.**

**Before.** After the cut, only the petals and ring moved for about 130 ms; the circle began to contract once the frame's reverse reached the dilation window.

title: This week in RISE: a public gate and NVIDIA in Live

beats.say: Two changes this week. A gate for public digests, and NVIDIA in RISE Live.
First, infrastructure. A Changes digest that another public repository runs now has its first security gate.
A run asks GitHub whether the repository is public. If it is not, the run stops before the index, the pull requests, or a model.
A name that is not owner slash name never becomes a request. The error repeats nothing GitHub returned.
Figures kit is the public mode. An illustrator brief is refused and can be repaired. A scene that carries code is not written. The weekly RISE digest may still ask the illustrator for a brief.

A callable workflow lets another public repository run this. It uses the pinned RISE commit and never installs the caller's dependencies. The model credential is present only in the step that runs the digest, and publishing never forces a push.

A digest from another repository cannot be shown on the Changes page yet, because the app still requires pull request addresses from RISE. And the Monday job now depends on GitHub's API saying RISE is public.
Second, RISE Live. NVIDIA is now a fourth keyed provider, listed as NVIDIA, your key.
It works like Anthropic and OpenAI chat. The reader's browser calls NVIDIA's chat endpoint with the key the reader typed. There is no Worker route.
The key travels in one authorization header. It never appears in an address, a log, the About page or an error. The key field is a password field kept in page memory only.
The default model is nvidia nemotron 3.5 lightning 30b a3b. Only the reply content is read, never the reasoning. A 401 or 403 means the key was refused, and the venue forgets it.
There is a catch. NVIDIA's API does not accept requests from the RISE site's browser yet. Its preflight answer carries no allow-origin header for the site, so the browser blocks the request.

RISE says so in a plain sentence under the key field, and keeps the key, since NVIDIA never refused it. A Worker relay would work, but it would send keys through RISE, which the rules forbid, so none was built. Changing that is the owner's call.
NVIDIA stays listed, with that warning.

## What

Adds NVIDIA as a fourth keyed provider in the RISE Live venue (`NVIDIA (your key)`), the same way Anthropic and OpenAI chat work. It's a twin of `openai-chat.js`, built on `keyed-stream.js`. It calls NVIDIA's OpenAI-compatible chat completions endpoint (`POST https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1/chat/completions`, `stream: true`) from the reader's browser, using the key the reader typed. There is no Worker route, no new client and no Realtime. Task record: `docs/product/tasks/LIVE-031.json`. Plan page: `docs/plans/LIVE-NVIDIA.md`.

- **Adapter** `src/live/adapters/nvidia.js`. It reuses `openai-chat.js`'s `wire` (now exported), so only `delta.content` is read and `reasoning_content` never is. Body: `max_tokens`, `stream_options.include_usage`, `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking: false`. The default model is `nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning-30b-a3b`, confirmed in `GET /v1/models` today. A model the reader names must match lower-case `publisher/name`. NVIDIA refuses with problem documents (`{status,title,detail}`), and a new optional `errorOf` hook in `keyed-stream.js` reads them. 401 and 403 both mean the key was refused (NVIDIA answers an unknown key with 403), and the venue forgets the key.
- **Key**: sent only in one `Authorization: Bearer` header. It never appears in an address, log, About or error. The existing scrub also covers anything shaped like `nvapi-…`.
- **Venue**: lists NVIDIA after Gemini. The key goes in a password field kept in page memory only, and the page says the key goes to NVIDIA alone. A new optional `note` on a registry entry shows one sentence under the key field (only NVIDIA has one; see the blocker below).
- **CSP**: `https://integrate.api.nvidia.com` is added to `connect-src` in both `netlify.toml` and `public/_headers`. `src/core/csp.test.js` pins that exact origin. `local/bridge.mjs` is unchanged, the same as for Anthropic and OpenAI.
- **Docs**: `LIVE-CURRENT.md` §7 and §9, `USER-OWNED-AI.md`, the new `LIVE-NVIDIA.md`, and the regenerated architecture diagram (module count goes from 76 to 77).

## Blocker: NVIDIA does not accept requests from this site's browser yet

I checked with `curl` and no key on 2026-10-26. An `OPTIONS` preflight to the chat endpoint with `Origin: https://rise.syberlabs.io` gets `200` with **no `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`**. With `Origin: https://build.nvidia.com` the request is allowed. So today a reader's browser on the live site blocks the request before sending it. The adapter turns that into a plain sentence ("Could not reach NVIDIA … NVIDIA's API lets a browser reach it only from NVIDIA's own sites today …"). The venue shows the same sentence under the key field before anything is typed, and the key is kept, because NVIDIA never refused it.

A Worker relay would make it work today. It would also send the reader's key through RISE. The registry's rule ("offered here only if its key goes from the browser to that provider and nowhere else") and `docs/USER-OWNED-AI.md` forbid that, so I didn't build one. Changing that is the owner's call. Another option is to hide NVIDIA from the venue until NVIDIA allows this site. I left it listed with the warning, but it's a one-line removal if you'd rather not show it.

| Shared conformance, including cut-short | `npx vitest run src/live/adapters/nvidia.conformance.test.js` | 13 passed (suite unchanged) |

pulls.title: Gate public Changes runs before any read or model call
pulls.body: ## Summary The first security gate for a Changes digest another public repository can run on its own machines. There is no endpoint on the RISE Worker, and no place a customer key is stored. A run now asks GitHub whether the repository is public, and stops before the index, the pull requests, or a model when it is not. A name that is not `owner/name` never becomes a request. The error repeats nothing GitHub returned. `--figures kit` is the public mode. An illustrator brief is refused and can be repaired, the same way any other composition fault is. A scene that carries code is not written. The weekly RISE digest is unchanged apart from the public check: it may still ask the illustrator for a brief. `.github/workflows/changes-public.yml` is a callable workflow. It checks out the pinned commit of RISE (`github.workflow_sha`), installs that tree, and never installs the caller's dependencies. The repository is `github.repository`, not an input. The model credential is the caller's secret and is present only in the step that runs the digest. The publish steps push `changes-data` on the caller's repository without `--force`. For any repository other than SyberLabs/RISE, the notification links to that repository's file. This app still requires pull-request URLs to be SyberLabs/RISE, so a foreign digest cannot be shown at `/changes`. ## How a public repository calls it ```yaml jobs: changes: permissions: contents: write issues: write pull-requests: read uses: SyberLabs/RISE/.github/workflows/changes-public.yml@<40-hex sha of this file> secrets: model_token: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN }} ``` ## Tests - `npx vitest run src/core/changes src/app/changes.test.js scripts/changes --config vitest.fast.config.js` — 12 files, 211 tests passed. - `node --test scripts/changes/digest.test.mjs` — 5 tests passed. The Monday job now depends on GitHub's repository API answering that SyberLabs/RISE is public. A failure there stops the run before a model call.

title: RISE this week: the live room, new figures, a cleanup

beats.say: This week in RISE: the live room, new figures for Changes, and a large cleanup.

RISE Live first. A first visit now says to ask about black holes and more, and offers three questions you can press. After you ask, the stage takes the focus, so Space and the other keys work. Figures now use the reading's own colours and font.

A beat that starts a scene and cues it now works, because the cue is retried for up to two seconds. And the account check now runs only for browsers that have signed in, which ends a console error for everyone else.
Maths is now typeset and spoken from one reading of each formula. The lowest energy, E sub 0 equals one half h bar omega, shows at the size of the words, and the voice says it that way.
A display equation appears alone and centred while it is said, and the voice pauses after a formula. Prices stay prices.
Two new choices in the room. Under OpenRouter, a Model field names the model asked, free ones included. And a quiet line now opens Who makes the pictures, with three choices.
A reading on a model that thinks by default now takes about one and a half seconds, not 23 to 54. RISE now asks for reasoning to be off. When a model's provider is down, the room says so honestly.
Free models now get visuals. In a room where only RISE draws, free Nemotron put a visual in 5 of 5 readings. Before, none of its 4 scene lines survived.

There is now a light room. In Settings, choose Porcelain: a warm porcelain ground, navy ink and a cobalt face. A word in the top-left corner of the home screen switches between the light room and the dark room.
Visuals made of light keep a night of their own. The attractor and the flame show through the face's aperture on deep navy. Figures are drawn in ink on the cream.
The Demo's line now reads Answered by Demo, and the eye is more restrained. The pupil moves inside the iris instead of the whole eye sliding.
The room can now hang photographs from reviewed collections. A design came first. Astronomy has 216 works, and landscapes and earth and sky followed, with 68 and 65 works kept.
Say show me astronomy and RISE answers at once, with no model call. The photograph carries a credit with its title, makers and licence.
After the owner's trial, the photograph now sits in Sophia's circle, one photograph per scene. Its credit is a caption under the circle. A paused reading now takes a named visual and plays on.
Landscapes and earth and sky open on the owner's favourites. A missing NASA credit is fixed too.
The words klee and night streaks now show Genesis and the attractor with night streaks.
Now Changes. Figures can be drawn in a company's own colours, and a new system figure shows how a change moved what flows between services, queues and stores.

A brand is only data: a name, a ground, an ink and an accent. One that would make a label unreadable is refused. GitHits is the first brand, provisional until it confirms its colours. No team is listed until its company confirms, so the live site shows nothing new yet.

The system figure draws the parts a change touched, the paths between them, and up to three states: before, after, and a rollback. Three real OpenStatus cases are kept as reference cases. Whether the composer picks it on its own is not yet verified.

Behind the scenes, four fixes. Cloudflare Web Analytics now runs and the Privacy Policy says so. The shared digest workflow checks out the right commit. Recitation retakes get new audio addresses. The Rijksmuseum gate reads the image's own rights.
On analytics: the site policy now admits Cloudflare's script. The Privacy Policy says the counter sets no cookie and uses no identifier, and that anything that did would be asked about first.
Old audio files stay intact, and a retake gets an address named from its own hash. A returning reader's browser is no longer stuck on a stale take. No production audio is regenerated.

Two more changes. Plus, Privacy, Terms, Apps and the Try entry screen now wear the Midnight theme of syberlabs.io, colours only. And a cleanup removed dead code in three rounds.
Two rounds removed about 22 thousand lines of unused files and exports.

A third round removed dead options and flags, among them the ASCII render language and an affect switch nothing set. Of 147 candidates, 102 survived verification and were deleted, and the reviewer restored none.

pulls.title: RISE Changes: a checked brand record, and listed teams' digests at /changes/<slug>
pulls.body:
Before: the figure kit draws only in the nine reading themes, on whatever ground the room shows. There is no way to draw a Changes figure in another company's colors. rise.syberlabs.io/changes plays only RISE's own digests; nothing plays an outside team's.

After: `renderFigure(spec, { brand })` draws any of the six kinds in a company's ink and accent, on a ground the figure carries itself, with the company's name as a wordmark above the title. A brand that would make any label unreadable is refused with its ratio, before anything is drawn. GitHits is the first brand, provisional until GitHits confirms its colors. And `/changes/<slug>` can list and play a listed team's digests from that team's own `changes-data` branch. No team is listed until a company confirms its brand, so the live site shows nothing new until then.

A brand is data only: `{ name, ground, ink, accent }`, each color `#RRGGBB`. Another key, a short hex, a color name or markup is refused. No SVG, font, CSS or code. The geometry, the type sizes and the six kinds stay the kit's. A theme and a brand together are refused.

To look at it:
- `src/core/figures/fixtures/*-northwind.svg` are every kind in one light brand (`#FFFFFF` ground, `#1A1A1A` ink, `#0B57D0` accent).
- `src/core/figures/fixtures/*-githits.svg` are every kind in the provisional GitHits brand.

## How

- **Full ink.** A brand sets every label in its ink at full strength, where a theme softens notes, details and subjects to 60–80%. This was the owner's call: a company's ink is chosen for its ground, so a mid-gray ink on white (down to `#767676`) passes.
- **Wordmark.** The name sits at label size (25 units) above the title, at baseline 30. It is set in the brand's ink by the same escaping `text()` as every label, so no kind's geometry or budget moves. A name too wide for the width is refused with its budget.
- **Contrast.** `brandProblems(brand)` checks every color a label is set in, on what it is set on, against the layout check's own `MIN_CONTRAST` (4.5:1): the ink on the ground, the accent on the ground, and the accent on its own 14% tint behind a changed flow step. Nothing is tinted to make a brand pass.
- **Layout check.** `svg-layout.js` exports `MIN_CONTRAST`, `contrastRatio`, `seenOn` and `parseColour`, so the kit and the check share one measure. One fix there: a translucent rect is now seen over the filled rect it lies wholly on, not over the room's ground. Before this, a light brand's changed step was measured on near-black and refused, though it reads on white.
- **Customer brands.** `src/core/figures/brands.js` holds each brand RISE draws in for a customer, reviewed in a PR the way the reading themes are, with its six kinds pinned as goldens. An entry carries `confirmed: false` until the company approves its colors.
- **GitHits (provisional).** Sampled from a phone screenshot of githits.com: ground `#13161A`, ink `#D5D9DF` (12.8:1), accent `#FF4FAE`, the pink where the wordmark's pink-to-orange fade starts (6.0:1 on the ground, 5.1:1 on its tint). The fade's orange (`#FF872F`, 7.6:1) is not used, because a brand has one accent. A screenshot can shift colors, so GitHits confirms.
- **Listed teams.** `src/core/changes/listed.js` maps a slug to another team's public repository and a brand. An entry is refused unless the brand is confirmed, so `LISTED` is empty. The Worker serves `/content/changes/<slug>/<file>` from `raw.githubusercontent.com/<owner>/<repo>/changes-data/` for a listed slug only; any other slug, a deeper path, a query or another method is a 404 that never reaches upstream. RISE's own `/content/changes/<file>` is unchanged, and `wrangler.production.jsonc` already routes `/content/changes/*` to the Worker.
- **The page.** `changesFromPath` reads `/changes/<slug>` and `/changes/<slug>/<id>` (a slug starts with a letter, an id with a date). A team's page is titled with its brand's name, its files come from its own path, and its digest is held to the same contract with pull reque

pulls.title: Check out RISE at the called workflow's own commit in changes-public

## What

`changes-public.yml` is the reusable workflow public repositories call to write their Changes digest. Its RISE checkout pinned `ref: ${{ github.workflow_sha }}`. In a called workflow the `github` context belongs to the **caller**, so that SHA is the caller's commit, which doesn't exist in `SyberLabs/RISE`. Every cross-repository caller fails at checkout, before the public gate from #730 runs.

`job.workflow_sha` is "the commit SHA of the workflow file that defines the current job" ([contexts reference](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/contexts)). GitHub's own example checks out a reusable workflow's source exactly this way. `repository: SyberLabs/RISE` stays pinned, and nothing else in the workflow changes.

`scripts/changes/public-workflow.test.js` asserted the old ref. It now asserts `job.workflow_sha`, and a new case refuses any `${{ github.workflow_sha }}` / `${{ github.workflow_ref }}` expression.

- New test vs. this workflow: **5/5 passed** (green), vitest 4.1.12

## What a person experiences
- Under **OpenRouter** in "Who answers", a **Model** field names the model asked. Free models such as `nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning:free` work at $0.
  - The field remembers the choice across reloads.
  - Empty means the default, `anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5`.
- A reading on a model that "thinks" by default now takes about 1.5 s, not 23 to 54 s.
- When a model's provider is down, the room says it is unavailable for now. It no longer says "OpenRouter has no model called … for your account".

## Root causes
- **Free NVIDIA testing.** NVIDIA's own API refuses browser calls from this site (re-checked today; LIVE-031). OpenRouter serves NVIDIA's Nemotron free and is reachable from the browser, but the room could not name a model.
- **Slowness.** RISE never asked OpenRouter to turn reasoning off, and Nemotron reasons by default.
  - It spent 2,000 to 4,096 hidden tokens per reading.
  - One reading spent the whole 4,096 cap and wrote nothing.
- **Misleading error.** OpenRouter answers a known model with no provider up with a 404, and the adapter read every 404 as an unknown model.

## What changed
- **`openrouter.js`**
  - Sends `reasoning: { effort: 'none' }`.
  - A 400 that names reasoning (a model that must reason) is retried once without it. Any other refusal is not retried.
  - A 404 is now `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE`, with honest words.
- **`registry.js`, `venue.js`, `LiveHost.css`**
  - The Model field, styled like the key field.
  - The room's adapter asks for the model at each request.
- **`app.js`:** the `liveOpenRouterModel` setting, which is text only.
- **Docs:** `USER-OWNED-AI.md` and `LIVE-NVIDIA.md` (the free route and the measurements). New task record LIVE-035.

- **Unit tests:** `npx vitest run src/live/host/venue.test.js src/app.safety.test.js src/live/adapters` passes 686 tests.

pulls.body:
The owner decided on 2026-10-26 to keep Cloudflare Web Analytics on `rise.syberlabs.io` and to revise the privacy promise honestly (option A), rather than add an opt-in switch. Task: FND-017.

## What was wrong

- Cloudflare auto-injects `https://static.cloudflareinsights.com/beacon.min.js` into the live HTML (confirmed by fetching the page). The site CSP `script-src 'self' blob:` refuses it, so analytics never ran and every page logged a CSP error.
- `PRIVACY.md` said "No analytics … no product analytics of any kind" and "if analytics were ever introduced — we would ask first."

## Changes

**CSP** (`public/_headers` and the mirrored `netlify.toml`; the Worker passes the asset header through). Two additions only:
- `script-src` gains `https://static.cloudflareinsights.com`.
- `connect-src` gains `https://cloudflareinsights.com`.

`src/core/csp.test.js` pins both origins, exactly, in both policies. `src/enterprise/headers.test.js` follows the new `script-src`. Tests were written first and seen failing (3 failed), then passing.

**Privacy Policy** (`PRIVACY.md` → `public/PRIVACY.md` and `public/privacy.html` via `npm run build:legal`). Last updated 26 October 2026; section 14 asks for the date plus a note in the repository history, which the commit message provides.
- The summary now says Cloudflare Web Analytics counts page views and load speed without cookies or an identifier.
- §4 gains a new "Page-view counts" section. It covers what a report holds, what the service does not do by Cloudflare's own description (no cookie or local storage, no fingerprinting, no cross-site tracking), that no reading text, typed text, question or key is ever in an address, how to block the script, and Cloudflare's documentation links.
- §6: "No analytics" becomes "Page-view counts only".
- §7 (Do Not Track): states that the page-view counter is the one third-party script and does not identify or follow you.
- §9: lists page-view counts in server processing.
- §10: legal basis is legitimate interest (Article 6(1)(f)). The "we would ask first" promise now covers any analytics that would set a cookie, use local storage, or identify anyone.
- §11: Cloudflare's retention (7 days unsampled, then about 10%; six months visible).

pulls.title: Maths seen and heard from one parse, in RISE Live and Composer (LIVE-032)
pulls.body:
**Draft on purpose:** the owner reviews before it can merge.

## What a reader meets

- **Before:** formulas in RISE Live showed as raw TeX in a small monospace face, a bare `\omega` sat mid-sentence, the voice read out dollars and backslashes, and "It costs $5 and $10" was typeset as the formula "5 and".
- **After:** "Its lowest energy is E₀ = ½ℏω, never zero." is typeset at the words' size, and the voice says "E sub 0 equals one half h bar omega". A display equation appears alone and centred while it is said. Prices stay prices.

## Causes, each fixed in its own layer

1. Live builds the Chamber from an answer's first beats, so KaTeX never loaded for formulas that came later.
2. Detection knew only `$…$` and `$$…$$`, with no money rule.
3. Nothing turned a formula into speech.
4. Live's parser rewrote every `|` as `/`.
5. A formula could be cut across two phrases.

## The change

- **One finder** (`src/core/math-text.js`): reads `$…$` (Pandoc's rule, plus a money test), `$$…$$`, `\(…\)`, `\[…\]`, TeX in backticks, and bare known commands.
- **One parse, two channels** (`src/core/math-typeset.js`): KaTeX gives HTML plus MathML; the Speech Rule Engine says that MathML in ClearSpeak. Its English rules are RISE's own lazy chunks, loaded through its `custom` loader, so it never fetches from a CDN.
- **Fallback** (`src/core/math-reading.js`): a plain Unicode reading for both channels before the load, or for TeX that KaTeX refuses.
- **Runtime:** holds a passage with maths until the typesetter has loaded (at most 3 s). The voice and the speech governor get the same spoken text, and the governor places each phrase exactly within it.
- **Chunker:** keeps formulas whole and gives a display equation a phrase of its own. Only the Current compiler passes it `mathSpans`, so nothing is added to the first load (63.1 KB against the 64 KB budget).
- **Look:** formulas are set at the words' x-height, so the line keeps its height.
- **Dwell:** a shown formula stays its saying time plus 300 ms per structure, that extra at most 2.5 s.
- **Model instructions** (Live) and the Composer guide are updated.
- **Dependencies:** `speech-rule-engine` 4.1.4, with `@xmldom/xmldom` overridden to the patched 0.9.12. The audit is clean, and `security:compat` now has the engine speak a formula.

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-26-math-both-channels-design.md`. Task: LIVE-032 (LIVE-031 is the NVIDIA task on main).

## Evidence

- **Unit tests:** targeted vitest runs pass (maths, compiler, chunker, atom map, runtime with maths, Chamber, system design), as do the Live runtime suites (about 760 tests). The fast list now includes the three maths files (162).
- **Browser test:** `npx playwright test e2e/live-mcp.spec.js -g "maths is typeset whole|a Current of beats plays in the self-contained card"` passes (2 tests), in Chromium against a production build.
- **First load and Worker:** `npm run measure:first-load` gives 63.1 KB, and the `wrangler deploy --dry-run` bundle builds.

- **A spoken pause after a formula.** `src/live/voices/pauses.js` wraps whichever voice the runtime makes. A passage with pauses goes to the voice in parts, the voice is held for each pause (300 ms per structure, at most 2.5 s), and the passage is reported as one, so the formula stays on screen through its pause. Hold, seek, cancel and pace all work through it.

pulls.title: RISE Live: the experience audit's six findings (LIVE-033)
pulls.body:
Task: LIVE-033.

These are the six findings from an experience audit of rise.syberlabs.io/live (headless Chromium, desktop and phone, reduced motion, a recording browser voice). The owner asked for all six to be fixed.

## 1. First visit
- **Before:** the entry invited "Ask anything.", and most questions ended the reading with "This demonstration can only explain black holes.", though the Demo answers five subjects.
- **After:** while the Demo answers, the field reads "Ask about black holes and more." and three Demo questions sit under it, each a press that asks it. The refusal names the five subjects and how to ask anything.
- **Where:** `src/live/fixtures/demo-questions.js` is small on purpose, so the entry doesn't load the readings.
- **Test:** every offered question gets a reading of its own.

## 2. Focus and keys
- **Before:** after asking, the field went and focus fell to `<body>`. The stage only hears keys inside it, so Space, R, F, the arrows and the pace keys did nothing, and screen readers lost their place.
- **After:** the stage takes the focus when a reading begins, unless the reader put it somewhere else.

## 3. Figures
- **Before:** a figure is drawn as an image, with neither the reading's background nor its fonts. The black hole the narration says "stays dark" was a white disk, and its label was in Times.
- **After:**
  - `class="dark"` fills a shape with the theme's dark (the background in a dark room; a deep ink in the coming light room).
  - Text in a figure that names no font gets the reading's face, carried in as data. This is proven to draw under the site's `font-src 'self'`.
  - The Demo's figure uses `dark`, the guide and the Live instructions tell models both, and the guide's example no longer forces sans.

## 4. A beat's cue and its scene
- **Before:** a beat that starts a scene and cues it gave the cue before the scene was on screen, so it was refused. That hit the Demo's calm and spin, and any Current that opens a scene with a cue.
- **After:** the cue is retried until the scene is up, for at most 2 s, and only the final outcome is recorded.

## 5. Account check
- **Before:** every visit, and every return to the tab, asked syberlabs.io who the reader is. For the many readers who never sign in, that logged a 401 console error.
- **After:** only a browser that has been signed in, or whose reader pressed Staff sign in, asks. A 401 forgets it.
- **Not here:** having the account service answer "not signed in" without an error status belongs to that service.

## 6. Smaller things
- The hidden "whole reading" transcript lists a passage once it's whole. Before, a passage still being written stayed empty or cut short.
- The Demo's interjection answer loses its "Good question:" opener.
- No change needed:
  - **"Ask →":** at full ink once its fade finishes; the audit screenshot caught it mid-fade.
  - **Empty paragraphs:** they're live regions, which must exist empty to be announced.

## Evidence
- **Unit tests:** `npx vitest run` over the Live runtime, voice, host, adapter, fixture, guide and figure tests: 73 files, 1658 passed. Account control: 23 passed.
- **Browser tests:** `npx playwright test e2e/live.spec.js e2e/account-saves.spec.js` against a local production build: 54 passed. One account test with its own mock failed; it was fixed in 87efc5f9, and `account-saves.spec.js` then passed (7).
- **Local preview probe:**
  - the stage has focus after a question, and Space holds the reading;
  - the Demo's three cues are accepted;
  - the figure's hole is dark and its label is in Crimson Pro;
  - no console errors, and no overflow at 390 px.
- **First load:** 63.0 KB against the 64 KB budget.
